plan: Ezekiel 32:17-32; Ezekiel 33:1-9, 10-20; Jeremiah 52:28-30; 1 Chronicles 4:24-43; 1 Chronicles 5:1-10, 11-17; Psalm 137:1-9

readings.title: Egypt's Descent to the Pit
readings.subtitle: A Wail for the Crowd of Mitsrayim
readings.text:
[17] And it came to be in the twelfth year, on the fifteenth of the new moon, that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[18] <dq>“Son of man, wail over <dn>את</dn> the crowd of Mitsrayim, and send them down to the depths of the earth, her and <dn>את</dn> the daughters of the mighty nations, with <dn>את</dn> those going down to the pit.</dq>
[19] <dq>Are you more pleasant than others? Go down, be placed with <dn>את</dn> the uncircumcised.’</dq>
[20] <dq>“In the midst of those slain by the sword they fall. She shall be given to the sword, drawing her and <dn>את</dn> all her crowds.</dq>
[21] <dq>“The mightiest among the mighty speak to him out of the midst of She’ol with <dn>את</dn> those who help him, ‘They have gone down, they lie with <dn>את</dn> the uncircumcised, slain by the sword.’</dq>
[22] <dq>“Ashshur is there, and all her assembly, with their burial-sites all around her, all of them slain, fallen by the sword,</dq>
[23] <dq>whose burial-sites are set in the sides of the pit, and her assembly is all around her burial-place, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, because they instilled <dn>את</dn> fear in the land of the living.</dq>

readings.title: The Nations in Sheol
readings.subtitle: Pharaoh Comforted by the Slain
readings.text:
[24] <dq>“There is Ěylam and all her crowd, around her burial-place, all of them slain, fallen by the sword, who have gone down uncircumcised to the lower parts of the earth, because they instilled <dn>את</dn> fear in the land of the living. And they bear <dn>את</dn> their shame with <dn>את</dn> those going down to the pit.</dq>
[25] <dq>“They have set her bed in the midst of the slain, with <dn>את</dn> all her crowd, with her burial-sites all around it, all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, for the fear they instilled in the land of the living. So they bear <dn>את</dn> their shame with <dn>את</dn> those going down to the pit. In the midst of the slain they have been placed.</dq>
[26] <dq>“There are Mesheḵ and Tuḇal and all her crowd, with all their burial-sites around it, all of them uncircumcised, slain by the sword, because they instilled <dn>את</dn> fear in the land of the living.</dq>
[27] <dq>“And they shall not lie with <dn>את</dn> the mighty who are fallen of the uncircumcised, who have gone down to She’ol with <dn>את</dn> their battle gear, and whose swords were laid under their heads. But their crookednesses are on their bones, because of the fear of the mighty in the land of the living.</dq>
[28] <dq>“And you shall be broken in the midst of the uncircumcised, and lie with <dn>את</dn> those slain by the sword.</dq>
[29] <dq>“There is Eḏom, her sovereigns and all her princes, who shall be given up in their might, with <dn>את</dn> those slain by the sword. With <dn>את</dn> the uncircumcised they lie, and with <dn>את</dn> those going down to the pit.</dq>
[30] <dq>“There are the princes of the north, all of them, and all the Tsiḏonians, who have gone down with <dn>את</dn> the slain, because of the fear they instilled. They are ashamed of their might. And they lie uncircumcised with <dn>את</dn> those slain by the sword, and bear <dn>את</dn> their shame with <dn>את</dn> those going down to the pit.</dq>
[31] <dq>“Pharaoh – Pharaoh and all his army – shall see them, and he shall be comforted for all his host that were slain by the sword,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[32] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have put a fear of him in the land of the living, yet he shall be placed in the midst of the uncircumcised with <dn>את</dn> those slain by the sword – Pharaoh and all his host,”</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Watchman's Duty
readings.subtitle: Warning the People of the Sword
readings.text:
[1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to me, saying,
[2] <dq>“Son of man, speak to the children of your people, and you shall say to them, ‘When <dn>I</dn> bring <dn>את</dn> the sword upon a land, and the people of the land shall take a man from their borders and shall make him their watchman,</dq>
[3] <dq>and he sees <dn>את</dn> the sword coming upon the land, and shall blow with the shophar and shall warn <dn>את</dn> the people,</dq>
[4] <dq>then whoever shall hear <dn>את</dn> the voice of the shophar and shall not take warning, if the sword comes and takes him away, his blood is on his own head.</dq>
[5] <dq>He heard <dn>את</dn> the voice of the shophar, but he did not take warning, his blood is on himself. But he who takes warning shall deliver his being.</dq>
[6] <dq>But if the watchman sees <dn>את</dn> the sword coming and shall not blow with the shophar, and the people shall not be warned, and the sword comes and takes any being from among them, he is taken away in his crookedness, and his blood <dn>I</dn> require at the watchman’s hand.’</dq>
[7] <dq>“And you, son of man, <dn>I</dn> have made you a watchman for the house of Yisra’ěl. And you shall hear a word from <dn>My</dn> mouth and you shall warn them for <dn>Me</dn>.</dq>
[8] <dq>“When <dn>I</dn> say to the wrong, ‘O wrong one, you shall certainly die!’ and you have not spoken to warn the wrong from his way, that wrong one shall die in his crookedness, and his blood <dn>I</dn> require at your hand.</dq>
[9] <dq>“But when you have warned the wrong to turn from his way, and he has not turned from his way, he shall die in his crookedness, but you have delivered your being.</dq>

readings.title: Turn and Live
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Plea to the House of Yisra'ěl
readings.text:
[10] <dq>“And you, O son of man, say to the house of Yisra’ěl, ‘This is what you have said, “If our transgressions and our sins lie upon us, and we pine away in them, how then shall we live?” ’</dq>
[11] <dq>“Say to them, ‘As <dn>I</dn> live,’</dq> declares the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> have no pleasure in the death of the wrong, but that the wrong turn from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! For why should you die, O house of Yisra’ěl?’</dq>
[12] <dq>“And you, O son of man, say to the children of your people, ‘The righteousness of the righteous man shall not deliver him in the day of his transgression. And as for the wrongness of the wrong, he shall not stumble because of it in the day that he turns from his wrong. And the righteous shall not be able to live because of his righteousness in the day that he sins.’</dq>
[13] <dq>“When <dn>I</dn> say to the righteous that he shall live, and he has trusted in his righteousness, and shall do unrighteousness, none of his righteousness shall be remembered, but because of his unrighteousness that he has done, he shall die.</dq>
[14] <dq>“Again, when <dn>I</dn> say to the wrong, ‘You shall certainly die,’ if he turns from his sin and does right and righteousness,</dq>
[15] <dq>if the wrong restores the pledge, gives back what he has stolen, and walks in the laws of life without doing crookedness, he shall certainly live; he shall not die.</dq>
[16] <dq>“None of his sins which he has committed shall be remembered against him – he has done right and righteousness; he shall certainly live.</dq>

readings.title: The Fairness of God's Ways
readings.subtitle: Each Judged According to His Own Ways
readings.text:
[17] <dq>“And the children of your people have said, ‘The way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not fair.’ But it is their way which is not fair!</dq>
[18] <dq>“When the righteous turns from his righteousness and does unrighteousness, he shall die because of it.</dq>
[19] <dq>“But when the wrong turns from his wrongness and does right and righteousness, he shall live because of it.</dq>
[20] <dq>“And you have said, ‘The way of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is not fair.’ O house of Yisra’ěl, <dn>I</dn> shall judge every one of you according to his own ways.”</dq>

readings.title: Summary of the Exiles
readings.subtitle: The Number of People Exiled by Nebuchadnezzar

readings.title: Descendants and Cities of Simeon
readings.subtitle: From Nemu'ěl to Their Dwelling Places
readings.text:
[24] The sons of Shim‛on: Nemu’ěl, and Yamin, Yariḇ, Zeraḥ, Sha’ul,
[25] Shallum his son, Miḇsam his son, Mishma his son.
[26] And the sons of Mishma: Ḥammu’ěl his son, Zakkur his son, Shim‛i his son.
[27] And Shim‛i had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children, nor did any of their clans increase as much as the children of Yehuḏah.
[28] And they dwelt at Be’ěrsheḇa, and Molaḏah, and Ḥatsar Shu‛al,
[29] and at Bilhah, and at Etsem, and at Tolaḏ,
[30] and at Bethu’ěl, and at Ḥormah, and at Tsiqlaḡ,
[31] and at Běyth Markaḇoth, and at Ḥatsar Susim, and at Běyth Bir‛i, and at Sha‛arayim. These were their cities until the reign of Daviḏ.
[32] And their villages were Ěytam, and Ayin, and Rimmon, and Toḵen, and Ashan, five cities,
[33] and all the villages that were around these cities as far as Ba‛al. These were their dwelling places, and they kept their genealogy.

readings.title: Simeonite Conquests
readings.subtitle: Expansion in the Days of Hezekiah

readings.title: The Descendants of Reuben
readings.subtitle: The First-born and His Forfeited Birthright
readings.text:
[1] As for the sons of Re’uḇěn the first-born of Yisra’ěl – he was the first-born, but because he profaned his father’s bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Yosěph, son of Yisra’ěl, so that the genealogy is not listed according to the birthright,
[2] for Yehuḏah prevailed over his brothers, and from him came a ruler, although the birthright was Yosěph’s –
[3] the sons of Re’uḇěn the first-born of Yisra’ěl: Ḥanoḵ and Pallu, Ḥetsron and Karmi.
[4] The sons of Yo’ěl: Shemayah his son, Goḡ his son, Shim‛i his son,
[5] Miḵah his son, Re’ayah his son, Ba‛al his son,
[6] and Be’ěrah his son, whom Tiglath-Pileser sovereign of Ashshur took into exile. He was leader of the Re’uḇěnites.
[7] And his brothers by their clans, when the genealogy of their generations was registered: the chief, Ye‛i’ěl, and Zeḵaryahu,
[8] and Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Yo’ěl, who dwelt in Aro‛ěr, as far as Neḇo and Ba‛al Me‛on.
[9] And he dwelt eastward as far as the entrance of the wilderness from the River Euphrates, because their livestock had increased in the land of Gil‛aḏ.
[10] And in the days of Sha’ul they fought against the Haḡrites, who fell by their hand. And they dwelt in their tents over all the eastern part of Gil‛aḏ.

readings.title: The Descendants of Gad
readings.subtitle: Chiefs and Clans in Gilead and Bashan
readings.text:
[11] And the children of Gaḏ dwelt next to them in the land of Bashan as far as Salḵah:
[12] Yo’ěl was the chief, Shapham the next, then Ya‛anai and Shaphat in Bashan;
[13] and their brothers of their father’s house: Miḵa’ěl, and Meshullam, and Sheḇa, and Yorai, and Yakan, and Ziya, and Ěḇer, seven.
[14] These were the children of Aḇiḥayil son of Ḥuri, son of Yarovaḥ, son of Gil‛aḏ, son of Miḵa’ěl, son of Yeshishai, son of Yaḥdo, son of Buz;
[15] Aḥi son of Aḇdi’ěl, son of Guni, was chief of their father’s house.
[16] And they dwelt in Gil‛aḏ, in Bashan and in its villages, and in all the open lands of Sharon within their borders.
[17] All these were registered by genealogies in the days of Yotham sovereign of Yehuḏah, and in the days of Yaroḇ‛am sovereign of Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: By the Rivers of Babylon
readings.subtitle: A Vow to Remember Jerusalem
readings.text:
[1] By the rivers of Baḇel, There we sat down and we wept As we remembered Tsiyon.
[2] We hung our lyres Upon the willows in the midst of it.
[3] For there our captors Asked us for the words of a song, And our plunderers for rejoicing, saying, “Sing to us a song of Tsiyon!”
[4] How could we sing <dn>את</dn> the song of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> On foreign soil?
[5] If <dn>I</dn> forget you, O Yerushalayim, Let my right hand forget.
[6] Let my tongue cleave to my palate, If <dn>I</dn> do not remember you, If <dn>I</dn> do not exalt <dn>את</dn> Yerushalayim Above my chief joy.

readings.title: A Cry for Retribution
readings.subtitle: Against Edom and Babylon
readings.text:
[7] Remember, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, against the sons of Eḏom <dn>את</dn> The day of Yerushalayim, Who said, “Lay it bare, lay it bare, To its foundation!”
[8] O daughter of Baḇel, who are to be destroyed, Blessed is he who repays you <dn>את</dn> your deed, What you did to us!
[9] Blessed is he who shall take And dash <dn>את</dn> your little ones against the rock.
